iut_type: End Product (smart communication unit with embedded antenna, Bluetooth V4.2 smart module, Seiko Solutions)
customer_question: Bluetooth V4.2's SIG certification appears to have a deadline around February 2026 — by when must we submit our application before that cutoff? This concerns both our current product and a second, future product (planned for later this year) using the same SM-M100 module, whose development schedule may not be ready in time.
question_variants: What is the actual application deadline for V4.2 before it's no longer registerable?
Is there a risk that our second, later product (same module, customer-handled registration) will miss the V4.2 registration window if its hardware isn't ready before February 2026?
actual_issue: Seiko Solutions believed Bluetooth V4.2 had a hard registration deadline of February 2026, and was concerned this would affect both their current product and a second future product (using the same SM-M100 module) whose hardware might not be production-ready by then.
plain_english_explanation: The customer conflated the Deprecation Date with the actual final cutoff. New registrations remain possible throughout the Deprecation period; the true final day to register V4.2 is the day before the Withdrawal Date, which is January 31, 2031 — far later than the customer's assumed February 2026 deadline. This applies to both the current product and the future SM-M100-based product.
consultant_answer: New registrations are possible even during the Deprecation period. The actual final registration date for V4.2 is the day before the Withdrawal Date: January 31, 2031. This applies to both the current registration and the planned future product using the same SM-M100 module — there is no need to rush either registration to beat a February 2026 cutoff.
decision_logic: Bluetooth versions go through Deprecation before Withdrawal; registrations remain valid throughout Deprecation, and only stop being possible on/after the Withdrawal Date. Customers often mistake the Deprecation announcement date for the actual hard cutoff.
final_recommendation: When customers cite a version deprecation date as a registration deadline, proactively clarify the distinction between Deprecation Date and Withdrawal Date, and state the actual final registration date explicitly to prevent unnecessary schedule pressure.
risk_if_done_wrong: If the customer rushed both products' hardware development unnecessarily to beat a mistaken February 2026 deadline, it could cause avoidable cost and schedule pressure, or conversely if they assumed registration was impossible after Feb 2026 they might abandon a viable product registration prematurely.
